claim: Every workstation unit execs one module inside `.git/trees/service-workstation`, and the pin reaches every `akasha/...` module that entry imports rather than that file alone. The worktree holds no `node_modules` of its own, but it does hold the repository's own `package.json`, whose `name` is `akasha` and whose `exports` is `./*`, so bun resolves a specifier naming the package it is already inside by self-reference, and tries that before walking up to the checkout's `node_modules/akasha` symlink. Command code alone still loads from the live checkout, because `calling.module` loads that by absolute checkout path. A run launched from the worktree therefore holds two copies of every module above that boundary, and module-scope state splits between them.

evidence:
MEASURED 2026-09-14, against the worktree itself rather than a replica of it.

BUN RESOLVES INTO THE WORKTREE. `Bun.resolveSync` handed `akasha/command/modules/calling/calling.module.code.ts` and a parent directory inside `.git/trees/service-workstation` answers that worktree's copy; the same call handed a parent directory in the checkout answers the checkout's copy. The same holds for `running`, `run-relaying`, `check-cost` and `command-stopping`.

THE LIVE IMPORT AGREES. Importing the worktree's `command/modules/cli/cli.module.code.ts` and the checkout's `command/modules/calling/calling.module.code.ts` into one process gives two different `calling` functions: the worktree entry got the worktree's copy rather than the checkout's. The namespace objects for `run-relaying` and `check-cost` likewise compare unequal across the two roots.

WHY THE EARLIER READING SAID OTHERWISE. The replica the previous finding rested on gave its pinned folder no `package.json`. Rebuilt exactly as that finding describes and run under bun, the replica prints `LIVE CHECKOUT`. Writing `{"name":"pkgname","type":"module","exports":{"./*":"./*"}}` into the pinned folder, which the real worktree has because the repository's own `package.json` is committed and a worktree is a checkout of it, makes that same entry print `PINNED TREE` with nothing else changed. That one file is the whole of the difference.

WHERE THE SPLIT FALLS. `command/modules/calling/calling.module.code.ts:262` loads command code at `join(root, beside)`, with `root` resolved from `AKASHA_ROOT`, which names the checkout. Everything above that line is the worktree's copy and the command's own imports are the checkout's. `infrastructure/service/modules/deploy-looping/deploy-looping.module.code.ts:92` launches every looped deploy through the worktree's `cli.module.code.ts`, so that split is the ordinary case rather than a corner.

ONE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE. With the worktree's `check-cost` reading the worktree's `spentRelaying()` while the checkout's `running` did the relaying, a run whose relayed child processor time was 0.124s was recorded as 0.070s rather than 0.194s.

NOT MEASURED. Whether a looped deploy relays at all: one real dry deploy through the worktree entry left both copies of the counter at 0.000, so the relay never engaged in that run. I did not read the entry modules of the other five worktree kinds.
